## [8.1.1](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/compare/code-review-action@v8.1.0...code-review-action@v8.1.1) (2026-08-24)

## Release Notes

The AI reviewer now correctly tracks which commits it has already reviewed — even when history is rewritten — so follow-up passes cover exactly the right scope and never drift due to stray reply threads.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

### Accurate Review Scope Across Force-Pushes and Thread Replies

Previously, the action anchored its "last reviewed" position on any review activity — including inline thread replies posted by the bot in response to comments. This caused follow-up reviews to silently skip commits that hadn't actually been reviewed, or to re-review too little after a force-push or history rewrite. Now, only *substantive* reviews (those that actually analysed the diff and submitted a verdict) are used as the anchor point. Inline reply activity no longer resets the scope.

The behaviour by scenario:

- **Unchanged head** — if the PR's head commit hasn't changed since the last substantive review, the review run is skipped entirely.
- **Fast-forward push** — the action reviews exactly the commits added since the last substantive review, nothing more.
- **Rewritten history / force-push** — because the old commits no longer exist in the branch, a full re-review is triggered automatically.

Each published review is now bound to the specific commit it analysed via `commit_id`, which is what makes the anchor reliable across rewrites.
